articles.title: Two kinds of political alienation pull support for violence in opposite directions, study finds
articles.summary: Feeling that your group is shut out of society is linked to support for political violence. But a survey in four European countries found that how people feel about politics can strengthen or weaken that link.

articles.title: New brain atlas reveals thousands of overlooked microproteins linked to Alzheimer’s disease
articles.summary: Researchers have mapped thousands of tiny, previously overlooked proteins in the human brain. This new atlas reveals that many of these hidden molecules are altered in Alzheimer's disease, offering new insights into brain aging and cellular energy production.

articles.title: The menstrual cycle may shape how much cannabis women use, new research suggests
articles.summary: Among people with premenstrual symptoms who used cannabis, the amount of dried flower they consumed tended to climb in the days before their period and again around ovulation, according to a study that tracked participants daily.

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? How should applied behavioral scientists navigate the financial and political influences on the work

articles.title: A simple cognitive reframing strategy reduces sensory brain responses in autistic youth
articles.summary: A brief lesson in thinking like an objective reporter reduced sensory brain activity in autistic children and teens exposed to scratchy textures in an MRI scanner, pointing to a possible new approach for sensory over-responsivity.

articles.title: Scientists identify two overlooked skills that predict reading success
articles.summary: A massive new study reveals that intelligence plays a surprisingly limited role in children's reading success, while visual processing showed no meaningful connection at all. Instead, the strongest predictors are sound recognition, vocabulary, and background knowledge, offering new clues about how to help struggling readers.

articles.title: The brain’s hidden fear mechanism may explain anxiety and PTSD
articles.summary: A surprising new discovery suggests that fear may cause the brain to blur the line between danger and safety rather than distinguish them more clearly. By observing brain activity in mice using augmented reality, scientists found that memories of threatening and harmless environments began to overlap, potentially allowing faster responses to danger. This "better safe than sorry" survival mechanism could help explain why people with anxiety or PTSD sometimes experience intense fear in completely safe situations.

articles.title: Extra weight may be aging your brain faster than you think
articles.summary: A major 24-year study involving more than 8,200 adults suggests that excess body weight may accelerate brain aging, leading to faster declines in memory, concentration, and decision-making skills. The connection was particularly strong among people over 65, raising concerns about the long-term effects of obesity on brain health.

articles.title: Early Stopping in Large Reasoning Models: A Survey and Empirical Audit of Efficiency and Reliability
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.00166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large reasoning models can improve accuracy by generating longer reasoning traces, but some of this computation may be unnecessary. Early-stopping methods aim to stop once enough reasoning is available to answer. Evaluating these methods requires accounting for the cost of deciding when to stop and the reliability of the resulting answer. We evaluate different methods across five reasoning models on mathematical and scientific reasoning, code generation, and factuality tasks by using a shared rollout replay protocol. We introduce Target-Integrate
